items.author: Ben
items.title: Construction draws materials - in the opening years, and as centres grow
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-26: 'we need those first 20 years of generation to include construction'. MEASURED CONTEXT: materials are authored per building (resource_costs) and charged at the build press, but generation PLACES buildings rather than constructing them, so the draw never fires during the opening years - stone and timber have a construction sink on paper and no pull in practice. TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that lasts: (1) make the opening years actually build, so the warm start carries a real material pull; (2) make POPULATION CENTRES draw construction materials as they grow, which does not decay once the warm start ends. An ancient economy's largest material sink is building, and half (2) makes that structurally true rather than transiently.

RE-MEASURED 2026-09-01, and half (1)'s premise has moved (NR-773 carries the fork). ERAS.md settles what 'the first 20 years' means: they ARE app::start_new_game's 80-tick warm start, not a separate generation pass - and the warm start now constructs. Ancient-band construction-channel demand, blind census -> surveyed (NR-772) -> surveyed with BL-711: 93.25 -> 202.58 -> 210.08; timber's construct draw 54.0 -> 118.3, clay 0.0 -> 13.3. Much of what half (1) reached for arrived through BL-711 (the AI could previously only ever build iron_ore mines) and NR-772 (demand_census surveyed nothing, so it measured a world where the AI built no mines at all).

WHAT REMAINS TRUE OF HALF (1) is narrower: the SEEDER's ~330 buildings are authored complete - `author_building` writes a default ticks_remaining of 0 (corporation_generation.cpp) - and draw nothing, ever. Fixing that literally opens the campaign with 330 half-built buildings, which is a gameplay change rather than plumbing, so it wants Ben's reading.

HALF (2) is unambiguous in intent and has a clean hook already in place: economy_system.cpp's BL-616 growth block, where pcc.population takes a step and ++pcc.scale promotes. The one open question is whether the draw GATES growth or only registers a want - NR-773 options A/B/C, recommendation C (want now, gating its own item), because BL-641's cliff is the standing warning: a brand-new universal draw unmet on tick 1 collapsed operating firms 198/328 -> 33/317, and gating growth on an unmet draw is that same cliff pointed at population instead of firms.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Roads, ports and hubs draw materials to stay standing
items.design: The infrastructure demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). The logistics_maintenance budget line already exists and names exactly this, so the state half has a home. THE WORK: a network that consumes stone and timber to stay standing - a permanent sink scaled by GEOGRAPHY rather than by population, which is a shape none of the other channels has. Second-order and wanted: it gives reach a running cost, so extending the network becomes a decision rather than a ratchet. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into LOGISTICS.md; the design register in MARKETS.md points at it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Government satellite launches - the tenth budget line, and space goods' first real buyer
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'add endpoints for space goods in government issued satellite launches'. Design in NATIONS.md section A budget. THE MACHINERY EXISTS - nations hold a weighted budget over priority lines, run_national_budget has claim/transfer machinery, and strategic_reserve is already a goods-buying line that no consumer claims on. THE WORK: a tenth line, space_programme, buying spacecraft_components and propellant through the BL-350 procurement seam (never on the open market - that is strategic_reserve's own rule). APPEND-ONLY: the weight vector is indexed by the enum and serialised, so the line goes last. Why it is worth more than a sink: state demand arrives in LUMPS and follows a weight a rival can lobby to move, so it is worth playing politics over rather than merely scaling into. ALSO OWNS spacecraft_components (BL-648's measurement, 2026-08-26): the guard's red list came back with ELEVEN goods, not the ten expected, and the eleventh is this one. Its exemption claimed BL-350 procurement, but procurement is a resource-agnostic TRANSFER between two corps' pools - it moves goods without consuming them, and admitting it as an injector would substantiate the entire roster at once. src/world contains no militia, and corp_ai.cpp says outright that the scorer does not emit those verbs today, so nothing automatic buys it. This line is its first real buyer.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Research consumes goods, not only credits
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'perhaps we could make research consume alternate goods as well'. Design written into RESEARCH.md. It gives the TOP of the production chain a buyer and turns the tech ladder into an economic decision rather than a free accumulator only time gates. Two properties: the basket is era-banded like every other, and a shortfall SLOWS research rather than voiding it (the same shape every goods draw takes). BLOCKED BY DESIGN on BL-619 (research system), which is a session with Ben - the rates, and whether the draw sits on the university or on the nation's budget lines, belong to that session rather than being settled ahead of it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: A battle consumes what it fires - conflict as a demand shock
items.design: The conflict demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). MEASURED: ordnance is priced at 43.00, near the top of the ancient roster, and its only draw is a per-head upkeep rate that BL-635's rescale took to 0.0035 - effectively nil. So the roster's most valuable military good has no buyer. THE WORK: a battle draws ordnance in proportion to what it commits, against the owner's pool, deterministically. WHY IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING OF THE EIGHT: it is the only channel that couples the game's two pillars - it makes Conflict move Trade, so a war somewhere else is a price signal here. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into MILITARY.md.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Tobacco, spices, coffee and furs get the buyer they were authored for
items.design: MEASURED: four endemic goods are on the roster, extractable, priced - and wanted by nothing at all, in any band. They pass the orphan check by naming 'mercantile demand', which BL-648 shows does not exist. THE WORK: a household demand that scales with WEALTH rather than headcount, flavoured by NATIONAL CHARACTER so different nations crave different luxuries. That asymmetry is the design, not a detail: it makes the trade route directional by construction - extract where it grows, sell where the money is - which is the most Trade-shaped channel of the eight and the one that most directly serves the pillar. Note it is also the first demand whose SIZE is a function of prosperity, so it rewards a player who has made somewhere rich.

items.title: A demand injector that cannot price a basket entry must SAY SO, not skip it
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE MECHANISM THAT MADE TWO SEPARATE BUGS INVISIBLE ON THE SAME DAY, which is why it is an item rather than a note. inject_population_demand and inject_background_demand both SKIP a basket entry whose resource carries no market base price - silently, with no warning and no row anywhere. Consequences observed 2026-08-26: (1) BL-649's census read as having no background demand at all on its first run, and (2) tools/verify/spawn_solvency.cpp - whose own header says it loads world_gen.lua and did not - measured BL-635's entire spawn diagnosis in a world where background demand did not exist. Neither failed. Both just quietly answered a question about a different world. THE WORK: an injector that cannot price a basket entry must report it - a named diagnostic on the first occurrence, and a harness row that FAILS on a basket naming an unpriced good, since that combination is always either a missing script or an authoring error and is never intended. A basket entry is a STATEMENT that somebody wants the good; silently dropping it turns a design statement into a no-op. Cheap, and it protects every measurement the rest of Sprint 21 depends on.

items.title: A short pool buys on the market, up to a reservation ceiling
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE BLOCKER UNDER BL-641, AND PROBABLY UNDER FOUR MORE CHANNELS. Measured 2026-08-26: with building upkeep rates on, operating firms went 227 -> 19, because the goods drawn are produced 0.0 in band and a POOL DRAW never reaches market_component::demand - so the want never becomes a price, no rival scores the building that would supply it, and the sink starves itself. run_construction and run_processing already bid; run_unit_upkeep does not and carries the same latent defect. DESIGN-OWED, and the open question is Ben's because it widens FINANCE.md: should a goods draw place real demand on the market when the pool is short - and if so, does it BUY (spending credits, which makes upkeep a market participant) or merely SIGNAL (raising price without a transaction, which is cheaper but invents demand nobody pays for)? The first is coherent and expensive; the second is a thumb on the scale and should probably be refused on the same grounds the project refuses clamps. Until this is settled, BL-641's rates stay at 0.0 and every remaining channel (BL-643 infrastructure, BL-644 state, BL-645 research, BL-646 conflict) should be checked against property 3 before it is built, not after. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-08-26): 'Buy on the market, but at a threshold, buying is not allowed. This goes hand in hand with maximum and minimum prices for goods.' And ONE RULE FOR EVERY GOODS DRAW - unit upkeep takes the same shape, not a second one. Written into MARKETS.md section Settled: a short pool BUYS, up to a reservation ceiling. THE WORK: a short pool bids the shortfall into market_component::demand and pays for what it gets; above the ceiling it does not bid at all and the existing shortfall rule weakens the building (or unit) instead. The ceiling is authored in the PRICE BAND family beside floor_mult/ceil_mult, not in upkeep - it is a statement about what a good is worth paying, not about who is buying - and its value is MEASURED against the census and the operating-firm count, never guessed. It is the exact mirror of BL-386's seller-side floor_price: both sides may decline a trade, neither may dictate one. Turning BL-641's rates non-zero is gated on this landing.

items.title: Spectator mode is reachable from the running game, not only from a --verify script
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "hopefully by the end of this sprint we can use a spectator mode to view AI playing in real time, and tighten core gameplay loops." This item is the route that makes that sentence possible; every other item in the sprint is watched THROUGH it.

THE GAP, MEASURED. `ui_state::spectating` has exactly ONE assignment site in the whole tree: `verify.spectate(on)` at src/core/verify_api.cpp:1096, bound behind --verify. There is no CLI flag and no in-game control. So spectate is today a headless-script capability only - the mode exists, is carried through to `corp_ai_params::spectating`, has a determinism harness guarding it (tools/verify/spectator_determinism.cpp), and cannot be entered by a person sitting in front of the game.

WHAT IT NEEDS. A route in, and honest behaviour once in. Two halves:
  1. ENTRY. A --spectate CLI flag is the cheap half and pairs with the existing --autostart family in main.cpp. Whether it ALSO wants a menu / new-game control is the design question - STARTUP.md owns the screen state machine, and a mode chosen at world creation is a different thing from one toggled mid-session. Toggling mid-session is the harder claim: BL-409's grant is written as a property of the SESSION (nobody seated), and flipping it live changes who the scorer may act on halfway through a run. Prefer entry-at-start unless mid-session toggling is separately argued.
  2. THE VIEW. `god_view` is the second flag and is the one that makes watching worth doing - it lifts the survey mask and opens rival internals (BL-408; read sites in body_surface_canvas.cpp, hover_content.cpp, selection_panel.cpp). It is gated on the PAIR `spectating && god_view` at every read site, so it is already safe; it needs its own control, offered only while spectating - time_panel.cpp:344-350 already has the shape.

DETERMINISM IS THE CONSTRAINT AND IT IS ALREADY PAID FOR. spectator_determinism.cpp asserts the two properties the standing rule names - the flag DEFAULTS FALSE so an ordinary played session is byte-identical, and admitting one more corp shifts no rival's cadence slot. Adding a route must not touch either. Re-run that harness as the verification, and do not re-bless its constant to make a change fit.

ACTIONS.json: any new control gets its entry, per the standing rule that a control change updates the dictionary.

items.title: The AI decision feed reports the real chosen candidate and its score, not 'overridden' at 0.00 on every row
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Raised as NR-626: every row in the AI decision feed reads 'overridden' with a chosen score of 0.00.

WHY IT IS FIRST AND NOT COSMETIC. The feed is the only window onto rival reasoning, and this sprint's whole method is WATCHING the AI and tightening from what is seen. A readout that prints the same thing on every row cannot distinguish a working scorer from a broken one - so every later item in this sprint would be tuned blind through it. It is the instrument, and the instrument is reading zero.

IT IS ALSO THE SURFACE THE NEW GOAL DEPENDS ON. AI_OPPONENT.md § The goal makes restraint a first-class move and calls the AI 'transparent by construction' on the strength of the decision log carrying a restrained move's REASON. A held move that prints as 'overridden, 0.00' is indistinguishable from a stall. Restraint that cannot be read looks exactly like incompetence, which is the failure mode the legibility requirement exists to prevent.

SCOPE. Find why the chosen candidate is not reaching the feed - whether the score is not carried out of the scorer, or is carried and not rendered - and fix it at the cause. `corp_decision_reason` already has a named-reason vocabulary (corp_ai.cpp ~line 285 renders 'workforce margin', 'recipe margin' and siblings), so the words largely exist; the question is why the feed is not receiving them.

OUT OF SCOPE: adding the 'held: already ahead' reason itself, which arrives with the margin term (BL-698, scorer margin term) and needs this fixed first to be visible at all.

items.title: The AI skill harness bands the spread in composite standing across the field, not absolute net worth
items.author: Ben
items.design:
AI_OPPONENT.md § The goal now makes a CLOSE RACE the intended shape of a campaign, produced by the world's brakes rather than by any agent's restraint. The instrument that scores the AI cannot see that quantity at all.

WHAT THE HARNESS MEASURES TODAY. Four per-seed metrics against golden bands: the net-worth curve (summed non-player balances), solvency ticks, survival fraction, and per-verb action counts. All four are absolute or aggregate. None can tell a run where every corp grew together from a run where one corp ran away - both sit inside a generous summed-net-worth band, and only the second is now a failure.

THE METRIC TO ADD. The spread between the leading corporation and the field, sampled on the existing SAMPLE_EVERY cadence. Held narrow is the pass; a widening gap is the regression. Exact form is the design call - leader-over-median and leader-over-second are both defensible, and the choice should be made against a real run's numbers rather than picked first (Rule 0b: report the observed spread with units, then choose).

THE ABSOLUTE BANDS DO NOT GO. They demote to a SOLVENCY FLOOR underneath the margin band. A world where the margin is beautifully narrow because every corp is broke is not a pass, and only the absolute figures can catch that.

CARRIED DEBT, and it belongs to whoever takes this item (NR-305): the current bands were blessed 2026-08-16 and are stale against everything since - possibly the mercenary contracts, the nation grants, or the roster widening. Re-derive from a fresh bless with dated provenance in the harness's own provenance-log idiom. Goldens here are disposable by project convention; the provenance comment is not.

ORDERING: this lands BEFORE BL-698 (scorer margin term). Building the objective before the measurement means tuning blind.

RETARGETED 2026-08-31 by Ben's systemic ruling. Two changes from the item as first minted:
  1. The banded quantity is the spread in COMPOSITE STANDING (BL-700, composite standing index), not in cash. Balance alone misreads the game constantly - a corp that just spent its treasury on a smelter is not behind.
  2. It is measuring whether THE WORLD'S BRAKES WORK, not whether an agent obeyed an instruction. No actor aims at the margin, so a widening spread is a finding about coalitions and climate, not about the scorer.

BEN'S FIRST-CUT TARGET, 2026-08-31: a leader roughly 28% ahead of the field. Treat that as the band to aim the SYSTEM at, not as a parameter to set anywhere - nothing in the code should know the number.

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: An opt-in margin dial scales a leading corp's whole candidate set - the difficulty knob, not the foundation
items.author: Ben
items.design:
DEMOTED 2026-08-31, the same day it was minted, by Ben's systemic ruling (AI_OPPONENT.md § Where restraint comes from). It was the sprint's centrepiece for about an hour. Read that section before this item - the demotion IS the design.

BEN'S OBJECTION, and it is correct: "The angle we are taking here is a literal handicap. I prefer to consider it as always a force from within the game system." A term in the scorer that says 'ease off, I am ahead' is invisible, uncausable and uncounterable. The player cannot see it, provoke it, benefit from it or fight it. It also buys its slim margin by making the AI worse, which § The goal forbids.

SO THIS IS NO LONGER HOW RESTRAINT HAPPENS. Coalitions (BL-699, rival coalitions) and climate (BL-701, living climate) are the foundation. This item survives ONLY as the explicit, opt-in DIFFICULTY KNOB Ben kept - "we can keep both modes" - and it is named as one, in the § 1 Area 4 sense of a small transparent economic handicap.

TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS, both from Ben, 2026-08-31.
  1. EVEN SCALING ACROSS EVERY CANDIDATE. Not a carve-out that discounts expansion and spares efficiency. Ben chose the even form deliberately over the surgical one.
  2. IT MAY NEVER VETO CONSTRUCTION OR EXTENSION. "'how far restraint goes' should never exclude extension and construction. If a player loses out, they should be able to see that the world doesn't wait for them." A dialled-down corp still builds, just less. A brake that freezes a leader destroys the honest consequence of falling behind, which is the thing the whole design protects.

OFF BY DEFAULT. The systemic route must be able to produce a close race on its own; if this dial is needed to get one, the brakes are the thing to fix. Ships as a mode, not as a default, and the harness bands the DEFAULT world.

Measured today for the record: corp_ai.cpp scores purely absolutely, and the only mention of `world::player_entity` is to EXCLUDE the player's corp (corp_ai.cpp:566-574, 625). Tunables live in corp_ai_params, per that file's own convention.

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: Rivals score stance against composite standing, so coalitions form against whoever leads
items.author: Ben
items.design:
PROMOTED 2026-08-31 from a nice-to-have to THE PRIMARY BRAKE. Ben: "With 7 corporations, we have plenty of room for alliances to form against leaders... I prefer if an agent's decision to slow down can be framed as usually motivated by systems." AI_OPPONENT.md § Where restraint comes from is the authority.

THE SHAPE. A rival's stance scoring reads WHO IS WINNING - the composite standing index from BL-700 (composite standing index). A corp near the top of the field attracts hostility; corps below it find each other worth befriending. The brake is applied TO the leader BY others, and no corp ever throttles itself. Every corporation keeps playing flat out; leading simply becomes expensive.

WHY THIS IS BETTER THAN A SCORER TERM, and why it is worth the extra difficulty: a coalition has a CAUSE, it is VISIBLE, and the player can join it, split it, provoke it or be its target. It converts the brake into gameplay. It also satisfies the standing rule that every system justify itself by feeding Trade or Conflict - a margin term feeds neither; a coalition feeds both.

THE VERBS ALREADY EXIST AND ARE UNUSED. corp_command.hpp carries four stance verbs from BL-448 - declare_hostile, offer_friendship, accept_friendship, return_to_neutral - specified, validated and serialised. corp_ai.cpp names NONE of them, so every rival is permanently neutral by omission rather than by choice. This item is the scoring that issues them; no new verb is needed.

THE PERMISSION EXISTS AND IS DATED. io-standing-rules.md carries Ben's 2026-08-22 grant for a rival scoring stance toward the player's corp, on the BL-450 terms - deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, legal verbs only, never a planner - and records that hostility stays a DECLARED state a corp opts into, never acquired ambiently. NOTE the provenance: BL-450 was PURGED in the 2026-08-23 cull, not completed; its prose is REFERENCE ONLY and this is authored fresh, per the cull's own resurrection rule.

THE COALITION MUST BE LEGIBLE OR IT IS JUST A HIDDEN HANDICAP AGAIN. That is the whole point of the reframe, so it is a requirement of this item and not a follow-up: a stance change emits into the § 7 chat channel and the decision feed, with its reason. A player must be able to SEE that the field has turned on the leader - and, when the leader is them, see it coming.

MUST NOT VETO EXTENSION (Ben, 2026-08-31). Coalition pressure makes leading costly; it never stops a corp building. See § The constraint on restraint.

OUT OF SCOPE: lobbying (nation-grain, purged as BL-539, unowned - NR-744), nation stance gating the player (BL-540, likewise), and the Stage C dialogue layer (BL-334, likewise).

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: A corporation's standing is a composite of economic, research and military power
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31, asked what quantity the margin is measured in: "It should be an aggregate of net worth, research, military strength... Maybe others too." AI_OPPONENT.md § Standing is the authority.

THE PREREQUISITE FOR TWO ITEMS, which is why it is minted separately: BL-699 (rival coalitions) scores stance against it, and BL-697 (skill harness margin metric) bands its spread. Both need the same number and must not each invent one.

ALL THREE COMPONENTS EXIST TODAY. Verified 2026-08-31 by reading the tree, because the backlog prose elsewhere claims research does not:
  * ECONOMIC - net worth: balance plus the assessed value of buildings and held stock.
  * RESEARCH - `science`, the corp research accumulator (BL-332, components.hpp:1343). Stockpiled, market-invisible, never decaying; REACHED, not spent. Already readable as a condition_set value (condition_set.hpp:77).
  * MILITARY - summed `unit_strength(world, unit_component)` over the corp's fielded units. COMPUTED, not stored: BL-459 removed the stored `strength` field in 2026-08-17, so read the function, never a field.

NOTE 'maybe others too' IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN by Ben. Build the aggregate so a fourth component is an addition rather than a rewrite - the weighting is data, and territory or market share are the obvious candidates if the composite reads wrong when watched.

WHY NOT BALANCE ALONE, which is what everything measures today: a corp that has just spent its treasury on a smelter is not behind, and a corp hoarding cash while its rivals arm is not ahead. A cash-only index would have coalitions forming against the wrong corporation, which is the failure mode hardest to notice because it still looks like diplomacy.

DETERMINISM. Read at a settled point in the tick and stable under the sorted-corp iteration order, or the evaluation cadence becomes the tiebreak. Name the read point explicitly and assert it - the standing rule's constraint on every scorer input.

WEIGHTS IN corp_ai_params, per that file's convention. Expect to tune them by watching (BL-695, live spectate route), not on paper.

items.title: Climate is designed and documented as the NEXT Era's catastrophe, outside prototype scope
items.author: Ben
items.design:
DOCUMENTATION ONLY, per Ben 2026-08-31: "Move BL-701 to just documentation - it's not the focus here." Filed the same day at difficulty 8 as a system build; it is not that, and nothing here builds climate.

IT TOOK THREE PASSES IN ONE SESSION AND THE CORRECTIONS ARE THE VALUE. Recorded so the reasoning is not re-derived:

PASS 1 proposed running climate through `tile_component.hazard_level` - static (written once at tile_generation.cpp:1962), already carried by the production formula's (1 - hazard) multiplier. REJECTED by Ben: "we will use a more detailed surface than hazard. Hazard is mostly just a tangible benefit for larger settlements on other bodies." One number per tile with one meaning cannot carry a body-scale state with several.

PASS 2 found the right surface - `planetology_state` unfrozen. Io already runs a physically grounded climate model at generation (the carbonate-silicate thermostat, the greenhouse budget, insolation, oxygenation, the arable calculation) and freezes the result. Climate change is a defined subset of those scalars moving: instellation, surface_temp_k, arable_share, life_stage, o2_fraction slowly. Fixed: endowment and the planetary facts. THIS SURVIVES. The dividing line is that climate moves what a world can SUPPORT, never what it is MADE OF.

PASS 2 ALSO got the era placement wrong, treating the nuclear war as a scheduled boundary event and climate as its aftermath. REJECTED by Ben: "The aim of each era is to give a catastrophe for players to avoid... I am not against climate change being a large problem for Era 2, but our prototype works solely on Era 1 for now."

PASS 3, WHICH STANDS. Every Era carries ONE CATASTROPHE THE PLAYER PLAYS TO AVOID, resolved deterministically from a watched scalar. The prototype Era's catastrophe is a nuclear war and its scalar is ALARM. Climate is the NEXT Era's catastrophe and its scalar is LOAD. CLIMATE.md is now written as that parallel, so the machinery built for the first rung - watched scalar, seeded test, red herrings with tells, deed-gated capstones - is what the second rung reuses. That parallel is what makes the Era ladder a system rather than a series of set-pieces.

THE ERA MODEL ITSELF WAS PROMOTED OUT OF RESEARCH in the same pass. ERAS.md § The point of an Era now carries the Ceiling/Alarm model, the test, the seven red-herring kinds, the tell-before-commitment rule and the inverse herring - drafted 2026-08-05 in docs/research/ERA1_TECH_LANDSCAPE.md and owned by BL-087, which the 2026-08-23 cull PURGED. The design was sitting in a research doc that is explicitly not authority. See NR-750.

KNOCK-ON, and it is the one that changes another design: AI_OPPONENT.md had named climate as the SECOND systemic brake on a runaway leader. Climate is out of prototype scope, so coalitions now carry that brake ALONE, and the doc says so plainly rather than leaning on an unavailable system.

items.title: God view has a control under spectate - ALREADY DELIVERED by BL-408, closed unbuilt
items.author: Ben
items.design:
CLOSED 2026-08-31 WITHOUT A LINE OF CODE. The item's premise was wrong and the control already existed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, on main before this sprint: `src/ui/time_panel.cpp:353` carries `ImGui::Checkbox("God view", &st.god_view)` inside an `if (st.spectating)` block, landed by BL-408 in commit 701cba55. It has its `chrome.sysmenu_god_view` ACTIONS entry, its `god_view_toggle` question-log entry, a `ui_elements.json` entry, and a visual check at `scripts/verify/spectator_god_view.lua`. Offered only while spectating, and a checkbox is a toggle by construction. Every requirement this item wrote was already met.

HOW THE ITEM WAS FILED WRONG, recorded because the mistake is reusable. The claim was "god_view is written in exactly one place, verify_api.cpp:1103". That came from grepping for `god_view\s*=` — an ASSIGNMENT. ImGui writes through a pointer: `&st.god_view`. So the grep was structurally incapable of finding the real control, and the absence it reported was an absence of a syntax, not of a feature.

THE LESSON, and it generalises past this item: a grep for `x =` does not find writes to x. For a C++ codebase specifically it misses address-of arguments, references, and member functions that mutate. Where the question is "does anything set this", the honest checks are the address-of form and the type's mutating surface, or a look at the one file most likely to own the control.

The slice agent found this in minutes by reading time_panel.cpp rather than trusting the brief, which is the behaviour the sub-agent discipline is meant to produce.

items.title: A watched run produces a written finding on how the AI actually strategises, into STRATEGIES.md
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "Our aim for sprint 26 is to ensure spectator mode works, and visibly watch AI play in order to further develop the meta." THIS IS THE ITEM THAT DELIVERS THE SECOND HALF OF THAT SENTENCE, and it is the reason the sprint is not just plumbing.

WITHOUT IT THE SPRINT CAN END WITH A WORKING SPECTATE MODE AND NOTHING LEARNED. That is the specific failure this item exists to prevent: three instrument items land, everything is green, and no statement about rival play is any truer than it was at the start.

THE DELIVERABLE IS PROSE, NOT CODE. A run watched end to end on the 1960s start (BL-705, selectable 1960s start), with god view on, and a written finding: what the rivals actually did, in what order, what they never did, where the scorer looked competent and where it looked blind.

IT LANDS IN docs/ai/STRATEGIES.md, which owns the meta and was AUTHORED AHEAD OF THE GAME - CLAUDE.md calls it "the meta, authored ahead of the game - research, not authority". This is the first chance to check that authored meta against what the scorer actually does. TREAT A DIVERGENCE AS A FINDING ABOUT ONE OR THE OTHER, not as a defect in the scorer by default: an authored strategy that no rival ever reaches may be a scorer gap OR a meta that was never real.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR, so the watching has a spine rather than being a vibe:
  1. Does any rival do anything that reads as a PLAN across ticks, or only locally good moves?
  2. What does the field's spread in composite standing (BL-700) do over the run - converge, hold, or run away?
  3. Which corp_verbs are never issued? A verb family with zero uses across a run is either dead code or an unreachable candidate.
  4. What does the decision feed's reason vocabulary actually say, once BL-696 makes it say anything?
  5. Where does a rival do something a human would obviously not do? That is the legibility bar from AI_OPPONENT.md § The goal.

FILE WHAT IT FINDS as NEEDS_REVIEW entries and, where warranted, fresh items - do not fold defects into this item's own prose and call it done.

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: A run exports a per-rival trace of what was decided and why, so a finding can cite evidence
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31, approving the proposal. Optional relative to the sprint's core - BL-703 (watch session finding) can be done by watching alone - but it is what turns a finding from a memory of watching into something that cites evidence.

THE SHAPE: a per-run, per-corp log of the scorer's decisions - the candidate chosen, its score, the runners-up, the reason, the tick. The data already exists inside the evaluation; nothing new is computed, it is a question of getting it OUT in a form that can be read after the run rather than only watched during it.

THE ADJACENT MACHINERY IS ALREADY THERE and should be reused rather than duplicated: `corp_decision_reason` is the reason vocabulary; the decision feed consumes the same stream; AI_OPPONENT.md § 8a's world history log (history_log.{hpp,cpp}) is the project's append-only tagged serialisation seam and already carries a `decision` topic. Check whether this is a NEW export or a READER over the log that already exists - the second is much the better answer if it holds.

DETERMINISM: the trace is an OBSERVATION, never an input. Nothing in the scorer may read it, and its presence or absence must not change a single decision - assert that a run with tracing on and one with it off produce the same state_hash.

IT ALSO PAYS FORWARD. AI_OPPONENT.md § 10d's corpus-generation direction is exactly this artifact: "every decision is logged as an input/output pair... those pairs are the supervised fine-tuning corpus", and § 10d notes the corpus and the replay log are the same artifact. Do not build the corpus here - but do not build something that cannot become it.

CARRIED OUT OF SPRINT 26, 2026-08-31, unbuilt and unscheduled. Ben closed that sprint at wave 1 once its own measurement showed every AI corp insolvent 29-30 ticks of 30 on every seed, with iron_ore produced 42991.6 against demand 0.000 on the industrial band (NR-758). This item's work is not wrong, it is UNMEASURABLE until demand exists: a coalition brake forms against 'whoever leads', and among corps that are all deeply insolvent the leader is merely the least bankrupt. Its tunables are the whole design and would need re-deriving against a solvent economy. Blocked on sprint 27's demand work rather than on any symbol - BL-642 names the first of it.

items.title: The 1960s start is selectable, and the campaign epoch reads world_params instead of a hard-coded constant
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "We will be working on the 1960s start." This is what makes that sentence executable. Sprint 26 watches the AI play, and BL-703 (watch session finding) watches it on a 1960s world - which cannot currently be started.

THE BRANCH IS ALIVE AND UNREACHABLE, measured 2026-08-31. `world_params::epoch_year` defaults to 0 and its own comment says the 1960 arc is deliberately kept working: "pass epoch_year = 1960 and it still runs, which is what keeps the parked space work buildable". The branch is real - `era_band_for_epoch` puts the recipe registry on the industrial band, `era_minus_one.cpp` skips the antiquity prehistory above 1700, and hard_coded_world.cpp branches on the same threshold. But NOTHING EVER SETS IT. There is no CLI flag, no wizard field, and no assignment anywhere in src/. Reaching 1960 today means editing a default.

THE SECOND HALF IS A REAL BUG AND THIS ITEM INHERITS IT (raised earlier as the epoch half of the two-clocks entry). `campaign_epoch_year` is a hard-coded 1960 in BOTH src/ui/format.hpp:82 and src/world/planetology.hpp:275, tied by a static_assert in tile_inspector.cpp, and format.cpp:134 computes the displayed year as day_tick/days_per_year + that constant. NO UI SITE READS world_params::epoch_year AT ALL. So today a 0 CE campaign renders 1960-based dates - the constant is simply wrong for the default start.

NOTE THE POLARITY, because it decides the order of work: moving to a 1960s start makes the hard-coded constant ACCIDENTALLY CORRECT again. That is a trap. Fix the constant to read world_params anyway - a value that is right by coincidence will silently break the moment either start is used again, and both starts remain supported (ERAS.md § Where the ladder starts).

SCOPE:
  1. epoch_year is selectable - the wizard is the natural home (STARTUP.md owns the screen state machine); a CLI flag is the cheap first cut and pairs with the --autostart family.
  2. The UI epoch reads world_params rather than a constant, and the static_assert is replaced by whatever keeps the two clocks honest once the value is dynamic.
  3. Whatever is stale on the 1960 path gets found by walking it - this is the first time anyone has.

EXPECT TO FIND THINGS. The 0 CE start has had months of attention and the 1960 path has had none since the arc split. Treat surprises as findings to file, not as scope creep to absorb.

items.title: Measure chain completeness per region, and the spread of it across the world
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "there is no reason that every start needs to be equally good and fair... If we send some of this work into generation, we should be making rules that encourage a level of asymmetry." GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § Asymmetry is the deliverable is the authority.

WHAT IS MISSING IS A READ, NOT A MECHANISM. Generation already has everything needed to produce asymmetry: planetology_state::endowment (per-resource deposit multiplier per body, 0.0 = the body cannot carry it at all), the endemic goods' latitude band x longitude sector, and the six-pass tile pipeline's terrain and deposit passes. What nothing does is MEASURE the result in economic terms, so nothing can say whether a generated world is varied or flat.

THE MEASURABLE: for a market or region, the fraction of the chains TERMINATING there that can be sourced within reach. The deliverable is its DISTRIBUTION across the world - wide, with real tails - not any individual region's value.

THE ENEMY IS UNIFORMITY, NOT SELF-SUFFICIENCY, and this is the whole point of the item. Two failure modes that look opposite and are the same defect: every region can close its own chains (nothing needs anything, trade has no reason to exist), or no region can close any (every dependency is identical, so one trade route is as good as another). Both are FLAT. A region that closes a whole chain by itself is a strong start and a legitimate outcome.

SO IT REPORTS, IT DOES NOT GATE. No start is clamped up to viability or down to fairness - that would be answering a multiplayer-ladder question this game does not ask. What it can legitimately assert is a floor on the SPREAD: a world where every region scores the same is a generation defect even when every region is individually fine.

HOME: demand_census is the natural host - it already walks every market and every resource per band, and it already knows which sinks are terminal. Adding a per-market completeness column and a spread summary is cheaper than a new harness, and keeps the before/after discipline sprint 27 runs on.

NOTE IT NEEDS 'WITHIN REACH' DEFINED, which is a real design question and not a detail: reach is LOGISTICS.md's, and whether completeness is measured at market grain, province grain or body grain changes what the number means. Settle that before implementing.

items.short_name: the ancient chain does not convert
items.title: The ancient chain does not convert - DIAGNOSED: the raws never enter the candidate list
items.author: Ben
items.design:
MEASURED 2026-08-31 with demand_census, ancient band, and it is a DIFFERENT failure from the industrial band's. Filed separately for that reason - the two bands need different fixes and conflating them is how one gets applied to the other.

THE ANCIENT BAND'S ENDPOINTS LARGELY WORK. BL-640's era-banded basket did what MARKETS.md property 2 asked: ceramics, dressed_stone, planks, leather, cloth and charcoal all carry real household demand. That half is not the problem.

THE MIDDLE IS. The chain does not convert:
  fibre    produced 27613.5   demand   89.7   price 0.756x base (near floor)
  leather  produced     6.8   demand   87.1   price 9.97x base, CEILED in 13 of 14 markets
  cloth    produced  4245.5   demand  178.6   price 8.87x base, ceiled in 11 of 14
  ceramics produced    63.5   demand  117.4   price 9.24x base, ceiled in 12 of 14

Raw inputs pile up at the floor; the finished goods the household actually wants are produced in single digits and price at the ceiling in almost every market. The demand exists, the input exists, and the conversion between them does not happen.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TUNING NOTE: a good ceiled in 13 of 14 markets is not a shortage, it is an absent industry. Something is stopping firms from being built on a conversion whose output sells at ten times base with unmet demand - which on the face of it is the most profitable thing available in the band. That is a question about the scorer's build candidates, placement rules, or the recipe graph, and it should be diagnosed before it is tuned.

CANDIDATE CAUSES, none confirmed - diagnose first: the input_demand_pull that BL-440 added may not reach these chains; placement rules may refuse the sites; the recipe may want an input that is itself unavailable; or the background-firm calibration (~90% of real demand, GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The economic premise) may be seeding the world without the converting firms and the scorer may not be adding them.

DO NOT FIX BY RAISING THE PRICE CEILING. The ceiling is doing its job by reporting the shortage; moving it hides the reading. Same reasoning as the project's refusal of clamps.

items.title: Power - generation buildings, a bought upkeep draw, and transmission on the road network
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "We should add upkeep costs of electricity, and power generation buildings." PRODUCTION.md § Power is the authority; LOGISTICS.md § 3a owns the transmission half.

POWER IS A GRID, NOT A GOOD AND NOT A POOL. Ben's ruling on how it moves: "Power travels via road infrastructure, although it is different from a convoy, it has a 1 qtr travel time or weight. So if there is a connection from a power source to the player's HQ, they will be able to use the power on the next tick. Power can be stockpiled, but not infinitely."

So: never on the order book, never on a convoy, no market price. Connection decides who can draw it. Stockpiled with a CEILING, which is its one genuinely novel property against every other good in the model.

IT NEEDS NO NEW GRAPH, and this is what makes it cheap rather than a second logistics layer. Connectivity is `tile_reach_cost` read as a boolean - FINITE means connected, INFINITY means not - so § 3's existing multi-source Dijkstra from supply anchors already answers the question. Latency is FLAT one tick regardless of distance, which is what makes it unlike a convoy despite sharing the road. And § 7's interdiction already severs the network, so cutting roads turns the lights off with no special case written.

WHY IT CLOSES THE FUEL CHAIN, which is the reason it is worth building now. coal and petroleum are both on demand_census's 'extractable, NO market sink' list - petroleum produced 6169.9 against demand 0.000 in the industrial band. The generator buys its fuel ON THE MARKET as an ordinary processing input, which already bids. So the chain is fuel -> generator -> power -> building upkeep, terminating in upkeep, and the market demand created is demand for FUEL, priced normally and scaling with however much generation exists. Power itself never needs a channel.

THE SHORTFALL RULE IS THE BL-641 LESSON APPLIED BEFORE THE FACT: a building short of power SCALES ITS OUTPUT DOWN, it is not idled. An upkeep draw that idles a firm kills the buyer that would have induced the supply, and the measured cost of learning that was operating firms collapsing 227 -> 19. A firm on reduced output keeps bidding for fuel, and the generation that answers it gets built.

INDUSTRIAL BAND ONLY (Ben, 2026-08-31). The ancient band gets no analogue - charcoal already carries real household demand there and is not an orphan.

POWER IS BOUGHT, AND SOLD INTERNATIONALLY (Ben, 2026-08-31, resolving NR-761 the same day it was raised): "it has to be a bought good when it is taken as upkeep. Therefore corporations can buy power from each other, and background companies can produce power with a profit... Even internationally."

SO BOTH LINKS OF THE CHAIN BID: the generator buys fuel as a processing input, every building buys power as upkeep. Neither is a pool draw, so neither severs the chain. Power upkeep is the FIRST channel built on BL-654 rule rather than an exception to it.

WHAT STAYS SPECIAL IS THE MOVEMENT, NOT THE MARKET. Power has a price and no convoy: transmission is the road network, flat one-tick latency, and a buyer can only match a seller its network reaches - which keeps the price regional by construction without any rule naming a region.

CROSS-BORDER NEEDS NO NEW MACHINERY: MARKETS.md section Tariffs already charges the enacted import duty on a matched trade whose buyer is domiciled outside the market jurisdiction.

AND IT REACHES ERA 1 CATASTROPHE. ERAS.md danger table names cross-border trade as the cheapest Alarm suppressant in the game, with Autarkic Substitution as the herring that cuts those ties. A nation whose lights depend on a neighbours generation has a reason not to escalate. Power feeds Trade and Conflict at once.

items.title: Construction becomes a sector with a throughput and a production method, not a per-building lump sum
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-31: "we should parameterize construction. We can use construction as a rate, and pay upkeep on construction buildings which costs (depending on production method). The costs can be wood, iron, steel, e.t.c. Very similar to Victoria 3 in my mind." PRODUCTION.md § Construction as a rate is the authority.

THE CHANNEL IT FIXES. Construction demand measures 0.000 in the industrial band because run_construction fires only where something is actively building - it is episodic, and when nothing is under construction the channel is silent. A sector makes it CONTINUOUS and ECONOMY-SCALED: capacity exists, draws its method's goods as upkeep every tick, and grows with the world. MARKETS.md property 1 satisfied by construction rather than asserted of it.

BEN'S OWN REASON IS THE STRONGEST PART: "This makes it easy to start with some construction of a certain method, and gives us an initial demand for those construction goods." Seeded capacity gives non-zero demand from TICK 0 in every market that has any - which is MARKETS.md property 5's 'every chain terminates in every market' delivered by the generator rather than by authoring a basket. It is also an asymmetry lever: a region seeded on timber frame wants different goods, and is differently capable, from one seeded on steel.

FIVE METHODS, era-banded exactly as recipes are: timber frame and stone-and-brick (ancient); iron frame, steel frame and reinforced concrete (industrial). Baskets and rates are MEASURED against the census, never guessed. The ladder spans both bands deliberately, so the ancient band gains continuous construction demand too - it currently measures 56.3, better than zero and still episodic.

IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ADDITIVE, and that is why it sits after BL-708 (power as a grid) rather than beside it. It reaches construct_building, placement rules, the build door, and the AI scorer's capex model.

NR-592 IS FIXED HERE, on Ben's call ("With the construction change - it must reason about a shared pool"). corp_ai.cpp never prices resource_build_cost when scoring a build; a candidate scores on cash alone and the seam refuses it at apply time. Under a lump-sum model that is a missed opportunity. Under a SHARED CAPACITY POOL it becomes a correctness problem, because capacity is CONTENDED: a scorer blind to it will propose builds the pool cannot serve, every evaluation, for as long as the pool is short - which is the same thrash shape BL-696 just measured in the recipe margin-chase.

MEASURE BETWEEN THE TWO ITEMS. Run demand_census after BL-708 and again after this, so what power did and what construction did can be told apart.
items.summary:
VERIFIED 2026-09-01 and DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. The code merged on 2026-08-31 (faf36725 / 26bc4fdd) and builds green, and the linter's false-open warning was right to say so — but the warning's own text is the correct reading here: *a partial slice can land under an item that is legitimately still open*. Three of four requirement rows verify; R1, the row the item exists for, does not.

R2 COMPLETE — five methods, era-banded, all group "Construction": timber_frame and stone_and_brick (ancient), iron_frame, steel_frame and reinforced_concrete (industrial), recipes.lua 827/842/857/874/889.
R3 COMPLETE — demand_census: `construction_capacity` is in the TERMINAL SET of both bands and priced in 14 of 14 ancient markets and 9 of 9 industrial, 0 floored, `in band` in both. MARKETS.md property 5 delivered by the generator, which is Ben's own stated reason for the change.
R4 COMPLETE — NR-592 cleared: `build_material_cost` is in the capex of both build candidates (corp_ai.cpp:951, :1202), keyed by recipe per BL-590. NR-592 marked resolved.
R1 PENDING — 'continuous and economy-scaled' is not what the world does. demand_census, ancient band: `construction_capacity` PRODUCED 0.0 over an 80-tick warm start with two timber-frame yards standing and both their inputs available (timber 5359.1, planks 635.8) — the yards exist and make nothing. chain_conversion_probe, industrial band: both seeded yards are GONE by tick 80, by removal rather than by switching (BL-712 confined the recipe chase to its own group, so it is not that). The census's `construct` column is still driven by live projects — the episodic behaviour this row was written to replace.

NOT AN OVERSIGHT, and that is why this is a known-hard row rather than a defect: economy.lua records that the obvious shape — capacity as a per-standing-building upkeep draw — was tried and MEASURED to collapse operating firms 198/328 -> 33/317, a cliff rather than a curve, the BL-641 collapse arriving through the cold start. NR-770 carries the diagnosis and points at BL-642 (construction draws), which owns the other half of the same fact.

Green on the way through: construction_harness, construction_gate_harness, upkeep_harness, and save_roundtrip at v22 — this item's own save bump, which had no working harness at all until BL-710 landed the same day.

items.title: save_roundtrip has not compiled since the mercenary tear-out - the save seam has been unverified across two version bumps
items.author: Ben
items.design:
tools/verify/save_roundtrip.cpp DOES NOT COMPILE and has not since cc88997c (the mercenary-contract tear-out). It references world::mercenary_offers, world::mercenary_contracts, world::next_offer_id and mercenary_contract_state, all of which that commit deleted.

WHY THIS IS PRIORITY A RATHER THAN TIDY-UP: save_roundtrip is the SAVE SEAM regression check, and TWO SAVE VERSION BUMPS LANDED WHILE IT WAS DEAD. BL-708 took v21 and BL-709 took v22, both on 2026-08-31, both appending to a serialised format, and neither was verified by the harness whose entire job is to prove a snapshot restores the world it was taken from.

That is the most consequential instance yet of this session's recurring pattern (NR-759): a check that is broken rather than failing, so nothing goes red and the absence is invisible. Flat binary serialisation is the project's chosen persistence (TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md refuses SQLite for it), which makes this harness the only thing standing between an append-only format and silent save corruption.

THE WORK is mechanical but touches SIX regions, and it is a repair rather than a deletion in only one of them:
  ~365-390  v6/v7 refusal tests whose COMMENTS reference the offers/contracts trailing sections - text only, verify they still describe the right versions
  519-520   P11 rejected-load check on mercenary_offers/next_offer_id
  747-748   P7 container-count rows for both containers
  782       P7 id-counter check on next_offer_id
  801-808   P11/P12 emptiness (inertness) checks
  920-944   the fixture that CONSTRUCTS two offers and one contract
  1076-1120 the field-by-field P11/P12 round-trip assertions

DELETE, do not repair: every one of these guards a property of a feature that no longer exists. The untouched-on-rejection contract stays covered for live fields by P3 and P9; the container-count table keeps its other twenty-odd rows.

A partial repair was started in the main session and REVERTED deliberately. This is the save seam in a 1100-line harness, at the end of a long session, mid-batch, and a subtly wrong deletion here - removing a row that was actually testing something live - is worse than the current honest breakage. It wants its own pass with attention on it.

AFTER FIXING: run it against v22 and confirm BL-708 and BL-709 round-trip, which is the verification neither item got.
items.summary: Six regions deleted, not repaired: the P11 rejected-load row, the two container-count rows, the two id-counter clauses, the two inertness checks, the offers/contract fixture and the field-by-field P11/P12 assertions. The v6 and v7 refusal rows STAY -- what they assert is the version contract, which cc88997c did not touch; only their comments were put into the past tense. Builds with `cmd //c toolserify uild_lua_harness.bat save_roundtrip` (NR-767: harness_params.hpp makes it Lua-linked and nothing said so). Runs green at v22: 63 PASS, 0 FAIL. Both dead bumps round-trip -- v21 (power) and v22 (construction_capacity) are resource_count widenings, 47->48->49, covered by P7's container equality and P8's byte-for-byte re-serialise, and v21 is refused by P20's symbolic `world_save_version - 1u`. That coverage is incidental rather than asserted; NR-768.

items.title: The world-level site pre-filter ranks on absolute deposit magnitude, so most resources are never candidates
items.author: Ben
items.design:
DIAGNOSED BY BL-707, 2026-08-31, with a probe (tools/verify/chain_conversion_probe.cpp) that is in the tree. This item is the fix its handover named.

THE DEFECT. `rank_extraction_sites(w, p.top_m_sites, demand_weight)` builds ONE ranked list of the top 8 sites FOR THE WHOLE WORLD, ordered by deposit x affinity x demand_weight, and every corp picks from those 8. Deposit magnitudes span three orders, so the list is homogeneous:

    1..8  iron_ore   12268.4 down to 7847.5  (the cut-off)
    best clay        205.7   NO
    best peat         75.0   NO
    best hides        507    NO

So clay, peat, hides, sand and fibre are never candidates anywhere, for any corp, in any world. Measured: extraction sites for those resources move +0 across 80 ticks while iron_ore gains +94 - into a good already glutted at 0.518x base and floored in 9 of 14 markets.

THE VISIBLE SYMPTOM is downstream and looks like a different bug: 30 Peat Kilns get built against 0 peat mines, 22 Potter's Kilns against 0 clay mines. The scorer is not broken - it correctly declines every candidate it is shown, and the only resource it is ever shown is the glutted one.

input_demand_pull DOES fire (clay 9x, hides 5x) and cannot help: it is bounded at 1 + 4*wanted/(1+sites) and cannot close a 60x gap.

THE TRAP THIS RE-SET. BL-440 fixed the TILE-LOCAL version of exactly this and its own comment names it: "Pre-selecting the richest was a TILE-LOCAL heuristic answering a WORLD-level question." It then left the world-level truncation in place, which is the identical defect one altitude up. See NR-765 for the third instance.

THE FIX SHAPE: rank scale-free (normalise within resource), or take a PER-RESOURCE top-K instead of a global top-M, so every resource reaches the scorer and the SCORER decides - which is what the scorer is for.

DETERMINISM-AFFECTING AND IT MOVES EVERY ECONOMY GOLDEN. That is why BL-707 handed it over rather than attempting it. Expect one deliberate re-bless wave with dated provenance, not a dribble (the NR-596 precedent).
items.summary:
`rank_extraction_sites` keeps the best K OF EACH RESOURCE instead of a global top-M. `corp_ai_params::top_m_sites = 8` is RETIRED and replaced by `top_k_sites_per_resource = 2` - 2 rather than 1 so a resource whose best tile is unbuildable is not silently excluded again, the same second-chance argument as BL-712's per-group build candidates. Buckets walk in ascending resource index, not `k_extractable` order, so registering a new extractable appends rather than reshuffles. One O(sites) bucketing pass; the per-bucket partial_sort keeps the old comparator, tile-id tie-break included.

MEASURED, chain_conversion_probe, 80 warm ticks, extraction sites gained. BEFORE: every non-iron resource +0, iron_ore +85. AFTER, ancient: iron_ore +30, water +10, petroleum +8, silica +4, copper_ore +3, clay +2, hides +2, timber +2, rare_earth_ore +2, agricultural_produce +2, fibre +2, coal +1, sand +1. AFTER, industrial: COAL +25, against 0 coal mines in any world ever - the canonical starved chain NR-766 named, and the input to the band's largest recipe.

DOWNSTREAM, demand_census (now surveyed, NR-772), ancient `produced`, surveyed-pre-BL-711 -> surveyed-with: coal 0.0 -> 632.7, clay 0.0 -> 349.1, hides 0.0 -> 353.9, sand 0.0 -> 35.8, and their converters follow - ceramics 24.5 -> 55.3, leather 8.0 -> 58.4. Four chains that were permanently zero are live. Every census assertion still passes.

peat is the honest exception: it reaches the scorer and BOTH its slots are placeable, and it still gains no site. Suitability 75.0, the lowest of any extractable, losing on the net^2/capex curve - NR-769's second seat, now located precisely rather than inferred.

GOLDENS. Green: corp_ai_harness, econ, corp_agency, corp_ai_predictive, construction, construction_gate, recipe_switch, build_spree, decision_trace, determinism_harness, world_determinism. Determinism itself is intact - spectator_determinism's own reproducibility rows (two independently built worlds, same hash) and all of R3 pass. The only red is R2's byte-identity against the frozen pre-BL-409 constant, which was already stale by 150+ commits (NR-752) and is BEN'S to re-bless: golden=E350DF2A50BF4BAA observed=90BFB27CB57CC308. NOT RE-BLESSED HERE.

ai_skill_harness moved and NOT for the better on aggregate, which is worth saying plainly. Net worth by seed, before -> after: 0 -823105.8 -> -457322.6, 1 -211696.4 -> -191399.1, 2 -1047871.7 -> -890122.9, 3 -188095.2 -> -484580.0, 4 +202611.7 -> -1089008.9. Three seeds better, two worse, aggregate worse; solvency ticks improve on three seeds and seed 0's survival goes 0.71 -> 1.00. That is the sprint's own thesis showing up as a number: rivals now REACH the whole resource field, and reaching more of a world that still has almost no demand means building more into debt. The 25 band failures are unchanged and stay known-red (NR-305).

items.title: A site takes its highest-margin recipe, so a cheap universal good is never produced
items.author: Ben
items.design:
FOUND BY BL-708 while building power, and it is the reason that item landed structurally incomplete. NR-765 is the finding; this is its fix.

THE DEFECT. `corp_ai.cpp` picks a site's recipe by max net margin: `if (n > best_net ...)`. Margins span three orders, so the argmax is a category exclusion:

    power                    net  3.98
    price-ceiled electronics net 290

THE CORP AI CAN NEVER BUILD A POWER PLANT. Not rarely - never, in any world, at any time. BL-708's first attempt collapsed the industrial band to 25 of 407 operating firms with power produced 0.0, purely because of this.

MEASURED AGAIN BY BL-709: `construction_capacity` is produced 0.0 in BOTH bands after an 80-tick warm start, while 28 ancient and 9 industrial sites stand under construction wanting it at a ceiled price. Two features landed on 2026-08-31 that the AI cannot build.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Both power and construction were designed as ECONOMY-SCALED sinks - MARKETS.md property 1, demand that grows with the world. They cannot grow: they exist only where the seeder placed them, so the scaling the whole design rests on does not happen. A cheap good cannot win an absolute-margin contest however badly the world needs it, and 'wanted by every building on the map' is exactly the profile of a good with a thin per-unit margin.

THE FIX SHAPE, same family as BL-711 (extraction candidate list is scale-blind): rank scale-free, or keep a per-CATEGORY best so an infrastructure good competes against infrastructure goods rather than against price-ceiled specialities. The scorer should choose between real alternatives, not be handed one.

SMALLER AND MORE CONTAINED THAN BL-711 - one comparison in one selection loop, no world-level list to restructure - and it unblocks two landed features. Worth doing FIRST of the two.

VERIFY: power and construction_capacity produced > 0 after a warm start with the seeder's own dial at zero, and the operating-firm count not collapsing (198 of 328 ancient, 121 of 415 industrial are the current baselines).
items.summary:
TWO argmax loops, not one. (1) The BUILD candidate now keeps a best PER `recipe::group` and emits one candidate per group, so every category reaches the scorer. Instrumented on the industrial band: `Power Generation` emitted 168 candidates and `Construction` 430, both previously ZERO. (2) The recipe margin-chase — the sibling the item did not name — carried the same defect plus two of its own: it used the BROWSE index as an ABSOLUTE recipe id (the NR-254 crossing the build door gets right), and its unrestricted argmax proposed cross-group switches that the SEAM HAS REFUSED SINCE 2026-08-16 (Ben's BL-434 retraction). One proposal per building per eval, so the refused proposal STARVED the legal within-group switch. The comparator gained target+recipe tie-breaks, since a tile can now emit several build candidates.

MEASURED (chain_conversion_probe, real Lua registry, industrial band, before -> after): total processing facilities after 80 warm ticks 268 -> 282; distinct recipes in use 14 -> 17; `silica -> silicon` 16->2 becomes 16->10; the id-space fix opened `iron_nickel_ore -> steel` (+4), `regolith -> steel` (+2) and `coal -> power` (+2), none of which were reachable before. demand_census: clay processing demand 32.0 -> 96.0, peat 5.5 -> 27.2, sand 5.3 -> 40.0, hides 0.000 -> 33.6 (a chain with no demand at all now has some); every census assertion still passes.

THE VERIFY CRITERION IS NOT REACHED and NR-769 says why: the exclusion has a second seat inside `net^2/capex`, which is an absolute contest (Power Generation peaks at score 31.9 against Advanced Fabrication's 1884). That curve's retention is BL-417 and is Ben's call, so it was not taken here. NR-770: construction yards go 2 -> 0 by REMOVAL, not by switching, and that is BL-642's. NR-771: ai_skill_harness returns byte-identical numbers before and after because its hand-built registry has three recipes in one default group — the sprint's success criterion is blind to this shape of change.

Green: corp_ai_harness (new R8, both rows, second row falsified by removing the guard), econ, corp_agency, corp_ai_predictive, recipe_switch, build_spree, decision_trace, world_determinism, determinism_harness. ai_skill_harness stays at its 25 known-red band failures, unchanged and NOT re-blessed (NR-305).

items.title: The build candidate score becomes an explicit linear metric - return on capital per tick, not net squared over capex
items.author: Ben
items.design:
STEP 2 of BL-417, resurrected from archive/backlog-purged-2026-08-23.json where the item had sat held since 2026-08-17. Step 1 (the honest rewrite, `net^2/capex` written out as itself) landed then; step 2 - decide whether the quadratic bias is wanted - was explicitly Ben's call and is taken here.

BEN'S RULING 2026-09-01 (NR-769, option A): take it now, linear metric, accept the golden reshuffle.
items.summary:
`c.score = (net / capex) * focus_weight * jitter * glut` at all three curve sites - the extraction build candidate, the processing build candidate (BL-712's), and the road candidate, which is priced UNDER the build curve by construction and would have outscored the site it exists to reach by two orders had it stayed quadratic.

WHY IT WAS FINALLY TAKEN: two independent fixes hit the same wall one level down. BL-712 put `Power Generation` and `Construction` in front of the scorer for the first time - 168 and 430 candidates against zero - and the scorer refused them anyway, peaking at 31.9 and 105.3 against Advanced Fabrication's 1884. BL-711 produced the same shape from the other side: peat reaches the scorer, both slots placeable, still no site. AI_OPPONENT.md's own § Selection must be scale-free condemns an absolute contest in as many words, and `net^2/capex` was one; the rule applied to everything except the score.

MEASURED BEFORE RESHAPING, 15,549 build candidates over one industrial warm start: quadratic median 13.54 / max 1884.33, linear median 0.106 / max 2.81. That put builds in the same band as their Nice-to-Have siblings (survey median 0.073, max 0.107) - an incomparability the quadratic had been masking rather than resolving. NO FUDGE SCALE was added to restore the old ordering: that would have been taking the change and cancelling it.

RESULT. Ancient band, extraction sites gained over 80 warm ticks: iron_ore +30 -> +13 (the glutted good stops hoovering slots) and coal +1 -> +17. ai_skill_harness net worth improves on three of five seeds and the aggregate slightly (-3.112M -> -3.041M), survival is 1.00 on all five, and the churn drops hard - resume 144 -> 60 on seed 4, 81 -> 40 on seed 0. Survey behaviour is unchanged: the feared takeover did not happen.

ONE HONEST RED, FIXED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: decision_trace_harness T2's anti-vacuity guard went red because the calmer scorer stopped overflowing the 256-entry ring (269 -> 207 pushed at 2400 ticks). The guard was right and its tick count was the problem - 269 against 256 is 5% headroom, and the rate is a property of the SCORER, not of that file. Re-measured under the linear score (2400/207, 3600/267, 4800/327, 6000/387) and re-sized to 6000 for 51% headroom, with a `--ticks` flag so the next scorer change re-measures instead of guessing.

Green: corp_ai, econ, corp_agency, corp_ai_predictive, construction, construction_gate, recipe_switch, decision_trace, determinism_harness, world_determinism, spectator_determinism (green for the first time in weeks - see NR-752). ai_skill_harness keeps its 25 known-red bands (NR-305).
